stem.en: A farmer wants a large number of genetically identical plants quickly. Which method suits this, and why?

text.en: Sowing seeds from cross-pollination, because seeds are all the same

feedback.en: Seeds from cross-pollination carry new mixes, so they differ.

text.en: Sowing seeds from two varieties, because they mix the best characters

feedback.en: Mixing gives variation. This farmer wants identical plants.

text.en: Spreading pollen by hand, because pollen becomes new plants

feedback.en: Pollen does not grow into new plants by itself.

text.en: Tissue culture, as plantlets are copies of one plant

feedback.en: Correct. Stem cuttings would also give copies, though in smaller numbers.

explanation.en: Asexual methods such as tissue culture and stem cuttings make new plants from one parent by mitosis, so they are genetically identical. Tissue culture gives many plantlets from a small piece.

hints.en: How many parents are needed for identical offspring?
Which cell division makes exact copies?
